title: A wartime cotton shortage and Kleenex (1914)

steps.claim: Kimberly-Clark develops cellucotton as a cotton substitute
The US military uses it for dressings and gas-mask filters

test.source: US Army and Red Cross use in WWI, 1917–18

steps.link_why: the military bought it as a surgical dressing

steps.claim: Nurses use surplus dressings as sanitary pads
steps.note: Company history; no independent primary record.

steps.claim: Kimberly-Clark launches Kotex
steps.link_why: Kotex was sold to use up the wartime cellucotton surplus

steps.claim: Kleenex launches as a cold-cream remover, later a tissue

test.source: Kleenex introduced 1924; marketed as a handkerchief from 1930

steps.link_why: Kleenex is made from the same cellucotton

title: A moldy cantaloupe and wartime penicillin (1928)

steps.claim: Fleming discovers penicillin, but yields are tiny
The US searches worldwide for a better-yielding mold

test.source: Florey and Heatley arrive at the USDA Northern Regional Research Laboratory, Peoria, July 1941

steps.link_why: the search aimed to make Fleming's discovery producible

steps.claim: Mary Hunt brings in a moldy cantaloupe from a Peoria market
steps.link_why: she was collecting molds for the search

steps.claim: Its strain, Penicillium chrysogenum, yields far more penicillin
steps.note: The often-quoted 200-fold yield came after later mutation work, not from the original isolate.
steps.link_why: documented in company, patent or institutional histories

steps.claim: Mass production reaches 2.3 million doses for D-Day

test.source: US production for the Normandy landings (American Chemical Society history)

steps.link_why: deep-tank fermentation of the Peoria strain's descendants

title: A horse's gallop and the movies (1872)

steps.claim: Leland Stanford wants to know if a galloping horse leaves the ground
steps.note: The famous $25,000 bet is a myth; the question was real.

steps.claim: Muybridge photographs a horse in motion
Twelve trip-wire cameras capture Sallie Gardner at a gallop
steps.link_why: the rig was built for Stanford's question

steps.claim: Muybridge projects motion with his zoopraxiscope
steps.link_why: built to show his sequences as motion

steps.claim: After meeting Muybridge, Edison files the Kinetoscope caveat

test.source: Muybridge's lecture and meeting with Edison, Feb 1888; Edison's caveat, 17 Oct 1888

steps.link_why: historians tie the caveat to the February meeting

title: A heat pump experiment and the Super Soaker (1982)

steps.claim: Lonnie Johnson tests a water-based heat pump at home
A custom high-pressure nozzle on his bathroom sink
steps.link_why: the nozzle was part of the heat-pump design

steps.claim: The blast of water sends him toward a pressurized toy
steps.link_why: his own account of the idea

steps.claim: He patents a pneumatic squirt toy
Larami launches the Super Soaker, a bestseller

test.source: released 1990 as the Power Drencher, renamed Super Soaker 1991

steps.note: The '$200 million in its first year' figure is widely cited but loosely sourced.

title: A failed angina drug and Viagra (1989)

steps.claim: Pfizer synthesizes sildenafil for angina
Trials at Morriston Hospital disappoint for angina

test.source: Phase I trials, Morriston Hospital, Swansea, 1991–92

steps.link_why: the trials tested the angina use

steps.claim: Volunteers report erections as a side effect
Pfizer redirects the drug to erectile dysfunction
steps.link_why: the side effect led directly to the new trials

steps.claim: The FDA approves Viagra; sales top $1 billion in its first year
